args.title: First win sets best time
args.description: With no stored best, a standard win becomes the best time.
args.given_when_then: Given no best time stored for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty

args.test_code:
import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


def _no_best_stored(difficulty_id):
    # Build the record as it is when newly created, then clear the stored best,
    # so that no best time is held for this difficulty.
    best = BestTime(
        id=f"best-{difficulty_id}",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-old",
        best_seconds=500,
        achieved_at="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    )
    best.best_seconds = None
    best.game_id = None
    best.achieved_at = None
    return best


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "difficulty_id, game_id, elapsed_seconds, achieved_at",
    [
        ("beginner", "game-b-1", 42, "2024-03-01T10:15:00Z"),
        ("intermediate", "game-i-1", 137, "2024-03-02T11:20:00Z"),
        ("expert", "game-e-1", 389, "2024-03-03T12:25:00Z"),
    ],
)
def test_first_win_sets_best_time(difficulty_id, game_id, elapsed_seconds, achieved_at):
    # Given no best time stored for this standard difficulty
    best = _no_best_stored(difficulty_id)

    # When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds
    best.record_win(
        game_id=game_id,
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        elapsed_seconds=elapsed_seconds,
        achieved_at=achieved_at,
    )

    # Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty.
    # There is no stored best, so the "slower or equal" rule has nothing to
    # compare against. The difficulty is standard and matches this record, so
    # the custom rule and the different-difficulty rule do not apply. The game
    # was won, so the lost/abandoned rule does not apply.
    # Expected: best_seconds == T.
    assert best.best_seconds == elapsed_seconds

    # The winning game is credited with the best time.
    assert best.game_id == game_id

    # The moment of the winning game is recorded unchanged.
    assert best.achieved_at == achieved_at

    # Identity and difficulty of the record do not change.
    assert best.id == f"best-{difficulty_id}"
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "record_difficulty, win_difficulty",
    [
        # Custom difficulty: custom games record no best time.
        ("beginner", "custom"),
        # A different standard difficulty: this record is not for that difficulty.
        ("beginner", "intermediate"),
    ],
)
def test_first_win_of_other_difficulty_sets_no_best_time(record_difficulty, win_difficulty):
    # Given no best time stored (same arrangement as the accepted case)
    best = _no_best_stored(record_difficulty)

    # When a win arrives whose difficulty is custom or differs from this record's
    best.record_win(
        game_id="game-b-1",
        difficulty_id=win_difficulty,
        elapsed_seconds=42,
        achieved_at="2024-03-01T10:15:00Z",
    )

    # Then nothing is created or changed: the custom rule / different-difficulty
    # rule decides alone, so the cleared best stays cleared.
    assert best.best_seconds is None
    assert best.game_id is None
    assert best.achieved_at is None

    # The record keeps its own difficulty.
    assert best.difficulty_id == record_difficulty

args.title: Lost or abandoned games record no best time
args.description: Only wins can produce a best time.
args.given_when_then: Given a game that ends Lost or Abandoned When it ends Then no best time is created or changed

import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


def _stored_best(difficulty_id):
    # Given: a stored best time of 100 seconds for a standard difficulty,
    # set by an earlier win (game "g-old").
    best = BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="g-old",
        best_seconds=100,
        achieved_at="2024-01-01T10:00:00Z",
    )
    best.events = []
    return best


@pytest.mark.parametrize("outcome", ["lost", "abandoned"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_lost_or_abandoned_game_does_not_change_best_time(outcome, difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id)
    before = best.to_dict()

    # When: a game of the same standard difficulty ends lost/abandoned after
    # 50 seconds, which is faster than the stored 100. Had it been a win, the
    # "new best time" rule would apply (50 < 100). Because it is not a win,
    # only wins can produce a best time, so nothing changes.
    best.record_game_end(
        game_id="g-new",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        outcome=outcome,
        elapsed_seconds=50,
        ended_at="2024-02-01T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # best_seconds: stored 100; a non-win cannot lower it -> still 100
    assert best.best_seconds == 100
    # game_id: still the game that set the stored best -> "g-old"
    assert best.game_id == "g-old"
    # achieved_at: still the time of the earlier win
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-01-01T10:00:00Z"
    # difficulty_id: unchanged
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id
    # no new best was created or changed -> no events recorded
    assert best.events == []
    # the whole record is identical to before
    assert best.to_dict() == before


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_won_game_end_with_same_inputs_does_set_new_best(difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id)

    # When: identical inputs to the lost/abandoned case, except the outcome
    # is "won". Standard difficulty, same difficulty_id, 50 < 100, so the
    # "new best time" rule applies: best becomes 50, game and time updated.
    best.record_game_end(
        game_id="g-new",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        outcome="won",
        elapsed_seconds=50,
        ended_at="2024-02-01T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # best_seconds: 50 < 100 -> 50
    assert best.best_seconds == 50
    # game_id: updated to the winning game
    assert best.game_id == "g-new"
    # achieved_at: updated to when the win ended
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-02-01T12:00:00Z"
    # difficulty_id: unchanged
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id

# test_spec_act_besttime.py
import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


ACHIEVED_FIRST = "2024-01-10T09:00:00+00:00"
ACHIEVED_LATER = "2024-02-20T18:30:00+00:00"


def _make(difficulty_id, best_seconds=100):
    return BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-first",
        best_seconds=best_seconds,
        achieved_at=ACHIEVED_FIRST,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "intermediate", "expert"])
def test_new_best_time_holds_exactly_constructed_values(difficulty_id):
    bt = BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-first",
        best_seconds=100,
        achieved_at=ACHIEVED_FIRST,
    )

    # Constructed from the first win: the values passed in are kept as-is.
    assert bt.id == "bt-1"
    assert bt.difficulty_id == difficulty_id
    assert bt.game_id == "game-first"
    assert bt.best_seconds == 100
    assert bt.achieved_at == ACHIEVED_FIRST
    # Nothing has been called, so no events were raised.
    assert bt.events == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "record_difficulty, win_difficulty, elapsed, expect_update",
    [
        # Standard difficulty, faster by one second (just inside the < boundary): update.
        ("beginner", "beginner", 99, True),
        # Same rule for another standard difficulty (each kind is covered).
        ("expert", "expert", 99, True),
        ("intermediate", "intermediate", 99, True),
        # Equal time (exactly at the boundary): elapsed < best is false, best kept.
        ("beginner", "beginner", 100, False),
        ("expert", "expert", 100, False),
        # Slower time: best kept.
        ("beginner", "beginner", 101, False),
        # Custom difficulty with a faster time: changes nothing.
        ("beginner", "custom", 99, False),
        # Different standard difficulty with a faster time: changes nothing.
        ("beginner", "intermediate", 99, False),
    ],
)
def test_record_win(record_difficulty, win_difficulty, elapsed, expect_update):
    # Given: a stored best of 100 seconds from game-first at ACHIEVED_FIRST.
    bt = _make(record_difficulty, best_seconds=100)

    # When
    bt.record_win(
        game_id="game-second",
        difficulty_id=win_difficulty,
        elapsed_seconds=elapsed,
        achieved_at=ACHIEVED_LATER,
    )

    # Identity and difficulty of the record never change.
    assert bt.id == "bt-1"
    assert bt.difficulty_id == record_difficulty

    if expect_update:
        # Same standard difficulty and 99 < 100: best becomes 99,
        # game_id and achieved_at come from the new win.
        assert bt.best_seconds == elapsed
        assert bt.game_id == "game-second"
        assert bt.achieved_at == ACHIEVED_LATER
    else:
        # Either elapsed >= 100, or the win's difficulty is custom / differs
        # from this record's: the stored best from game-first stays.
        assert bt.best_seconds == 100
        assert bt.game_id == "game-first"
        assert bt.achieved_at == ACHIEVED_FIRST

import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


STORED_BEST = 100
STORED_GAME_ID = "game-old"
STORED_ACHIEVED_AT = "2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00"
NEW_GAME_ID = "game-new"
NEW_ACHIEVED_AT = "2024-02-01T12:30:00+00:00"


def _stored_best(difficulty_id: str) -> BestTime:
    return BestTime(
        id="best-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id=STORED_GAME_ID,
        best_seconds=STORED_BEST,
        achieved_at=STORED_ACHIEVED_AT,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_win_just_faster_than_stored_best_replaces_it(difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id)

    best.record_win(
        game_id=NEW_GAME_ID,
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        elapsed_seconds=STORED_BEST - 1,
        achieved_at=NEW_ACHIEVED_AT,
    )

    # The record's difficulty is standard (beginner or expert), so the
    # custom-difficulty rule does not apply. The win has the same difficulty_id
    # as the record, and the game was won, so the lost/abandoned rule does not
    # apply. Elapsed is 99 and the stored best is 100. Since 99 < 100, the
    # "slower or equal keeps best" rule does not apply. So the best time
    # becomes 99.
    assert best.best_seconds == STORED_BEST - 1
    # When the best time is replaced, the game_id is taken from the new win.
    assert best.game_id == NEW_GAME_ID
    # When the best time is replaced, achieved_at is taken from the new win.
    assert best.achieved_at == NEW_ACHIEVED_AT
    # The difficulty of the record is unchanged.
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_win_exactly_equal_to_stored_best_does_not_replace_it(difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id)

    best.record_win(
        game_id=NEW_GAME_ID,
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        elapsed_seconds=STORED_BEST,
        achieved_at=NEW_ACHIEVED_AT,
    )

    # This case uses the same standard difficulty, the same matching
    # difficulty_id and the same won game as the accepted case. Only the

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


STANDARD_DIFFICULTIES = ["beginner", "intermediate", "expert"]


def _stored_best(difficulty_id: str, best_seconds: int) -> BestTime:
    # Given: a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty,
    # recorded from an earlier game "game-old" at a fixed time.
    return BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-old",
        best_seconds=best_seconds,
        achieved_at="2024-01-01T10:00:00Z",
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", STANDARD_DIFFICULTIES)
def test_equal_win_keeps_stored_best(difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id, 100)

    # When: the player wins a game of the same difficulty in exactly B seconds.
    best.record_win(
        game_id="game-new",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        elapsed_seconds=100,
        achieved_at="2024-02-01T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # Stored best is 100 and the win took 100: 100 < 100 is false, so this is
    # not a new best. Difficulty is standard and matches the record, so the
    # custom rule does not apply; it is a win, so the lost/abandoned rule does
    # not apply. The best stays 100.
    assert best.best_seconds == 100
    # The best was not replaced, so it still belongs to the original game.
    assert best.game_id == "game-old"
    # The best was not replaced, so its achieved_at is the original one.
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-01-01T10:00:00Z"
    # Difficulty of the record never changes.
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", STANDARD_DIFFICULTIES)
def test_slower_win_keeps_stored_best(difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id, 100)

    # When: the player wins a game of the same difficulty in B + 1 seconds.
    best.record_win(
        game_id="game-new",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        elapsed_seconds=101,
        achieved_at="2024-02-01T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # Stored best is 100 and the win took 101: 101 < 100 is false, so the
    # slower time does not replace the best. The best stays 100.
    assert best.best_seconds == 100
    # Not replaced, so the original game remains the holder.
    assert best.game_id == "game-old"
    # Not replaced, so the original achieved_at remains.
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-01-01T10:00:00Z"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", STANDARD_DIFFICULTIES)

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


def _stored_best(difficulty_id: str) -> BestTime:
    # Given: a stored best time of 100 seconds for a standard difficulty,
    # recorded from game "game-first" at a fixed time, with no events.
    return BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-first",
        best_seconds=100,
        achieved_at="2024-01-01T10:00:00Z",
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("stored_difficulty", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_custom_win_does_not_change_best_time(stored_difficulty):
    best = _stored_best(stored_difficulty)

    # When: a game on Custom difficulty is won faster than the stored best.
    # The game is Won, so the "lost or abandoned" rule does not apply.
    best.record_win(
        game_id="game-custom",
        difficulty_id="custom",
        elapsed_seconds=50,
        achieved_at="2024-01-02T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # Then: custom difficulty changes nothing. 50 < 100 would beat the record
    # for a standard difficulty, so only the custom rule keeps it at 100.
    assert best.best_seconds == 100
    # The game that holds the record is still the first one.
    assert best.game_id == "game-first"
    # The time the record was achieved is unchanged.
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-01-01T10:00:00Z"
    # The record still belongs to its standard difficulty, not "custom".
    assert best.difficulty_id == stored_difficulty
    # The record keeps its id.
    assert best.id == "bt-1"
    # Nothing happened, so no events are recorded.
    assert best.events == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("stored_difficulty", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_same_faster_win_on_standard_difficulty_does_update_best_time(stored_difficulty):

        difficulty_id=stored_difficulty,
        elapsed_seconds=50,
        achieved_at="2024-01-02T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # Then: standard difficulty and 50 < 100, so the new best is 50.
    assert best.best_seconds == 50
    # The record now points at the game that set the new best.
    assert best.game_id == "game-custom"
    # The achievement time is that of the new best.
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-01-02T12:00:00Z"
    # The difficulty stays the same standard difficulty.
    assert best.difficulty_id == stored_difficulty

import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


def _no_best_stored(difficulty_id):
    # Build the record as it is when newly created, then clear the stored best,
    # so that no best time is held for this difficulty.
    best = BestTime(
        id=f"best-{difficulty_id}",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-old",
        best_seconds=500,
        achieved_at="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    )
    best.best_seconds = None
    best.game_id = None
    best.achieved_at = None
    return best


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "difficulty_id, game_id, elapsed_seconds, achieved_at",
    [
        ("beginner", "game-b-1", 42, "2024-03-01T10:15:00Z"),
        ("intermediate", "game-i-1", 137, "2024-03-02T11:20:00Z"),
        ("expert", "game-e-1", 389, "2024-03-03T12:25:00Z"),
    ],
)
def test_first_win_sets_best_time(difficulty_id, game_id, elapsed_seconds, achieved_at):
    # Given no best time stored for this standard difficulty
    best = _no_best_stored(difficulty_id)

    # When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds
    best.record_win(
        game_id=game_id,
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        elapsed_seconds=elapsed_seconds,
        achieved_at=achieved_at,
    )

    # Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty.
    # There is no stored best, so the "slower or equal" rule has nothing to
    # compare against. The difficulty is standard and matches this record, so
    # the custom rule and the different-difficulty rule do not apply. The game
    # was won, so the lost/abandoned rule does not apply.
    # Expected: best_seconds == T.
    assert best.best_seconds == elapsed_seconds

    # The winning game is credited with the best time.
    assert best.game_id == game_id

    # The moment of the winning game is recorded unchanged.
    assert best.achieved_at == achieved_at

    # Identity and difficulty of the record do not change.
    assert best.id == f"best-{difficulty_id}"
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "record_difficulty, win_difficulty",
    [
        # Custom difficulty: custom games record no best time.
        ("beginner", "custom"),
        # A different standard difficulty: this record is not for that difficulty.
        ("beginner", "intermediate"),
    ],
)
def test_first_win_of_other_difficulty_sets_no_best_time(record_difficulty, win_difficulty):
    # Given no best time stored (same arrangement as the accepted case)
    best = _no_best_stored(record_difficulty)

    # When a win arrives whose difficulty is custom or differs from this record's
    best.record_win(
        game_id="game-b-1",
        difficulty_id=win_difficulty,
        elapsed_seconds=42,
        achieved_at="2024-03-01T10:15:00Z",
    )

    # Then nothing is created or changed: the custom rule / different-difficulty
    # rule decides alone, so the cleared best stays cleared.
    assert best.best_seconds is None
    assert best.game_id is None
    assert best.achieved_at is None

    # The record keeps its own difficulty.
    assert best.difficulty_id == record_difficulty

import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


def _stored_best(difficulty_id):
    # Given: a stored best time of 100 seconds for a standard difficulty,
    # set by an earlier win (game "g-old").
    best = BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="g-old",
        best_seconds=100,
        achieved_at="2024-01-01T10:00:00Z",
    )
    best.events = []
    return best


@pytest.mark.parametrize("outcome", ["lost", "abandoned"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_lost_or_abandoned_game_does_not_change_best_time(outcome, difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id)
    before = best.to_dict()

    # When: a game of the same standard difficulty ends lost/abandoned after
    # 50 seconds, which is faster than the stored 100. Had it been a win, the
    # "new best time" rule would apply (50 < 100). Because it is not a win,
    # only wins can produce a best time, so nothing changes.
    best.record_game_end(
        game_id="g-new",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        outcome=outcome,
        elapsed_seconds=50,
        ended_at="2024-02-01T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # best_seconds: stored 100; a non-win cannot lower it -> still 100
    assert best.best_seconds == 100
    # game_id: still the game that set the stored best -> "g-old"
    assert best.game_id == "g-old"
    # achieved_at: still the time of the earlier win
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-01-01T10:00:00Z"
    # difficulty_id: unchanged
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id
    # no new best was created or changed -> no events recorded
    assert best.events == []
    # the whole record is identical to before
    assert best.to_dict() == before


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "expert"])
def test_won_game_end_with_same_inputs_does_set_new_best(difficulty_id):
    best = _stored_best(difficulty_id)

    # When: identical inputs to the lost/abandoned case, except the outcome
    # is "won". Standard difficulty, same difficulty_id, 50 < 100, so the
    # "new best time" rule applies: best becomes 50, game and time updated.
    best.record_game_end(
        game_id="g-new",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        outcome="won",
        elapsed_seconds=50,
        ended_at="2024-02-01T12:00:00Z",
    )

    # best_seconds: 50 < 100 -> 50
    assert best.best_seconds == 50
    # game_id: updated to the winning game
    assert best.game_id == "g-new"
    # achieved_at: updated to when the win ended
    assert best.achieved_at == "2024-02-01T12:00:00Z"
    # difficulty_id: unchanged
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id
